# How to Merge Last Two Commits in Git

There are several ways to combine the last two commits. Here are the most common methods:

## Method 1: Interactive Rebase (Recommended)

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

This will open an editor showing:
```
pick abc1234 Second-to-last commit message
pick def5678 Last commit message
```

Change the second line from `pick` to `squash` (or just `s`):
```
pick abc1234 Second-to-last commit message
squash def5678 Last commit message
```

Save and close. You'll then be prompted to edit the combined commit message.

## Method 2: Soft Reset (Quick & Simple)

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git commit --amend
```

This:
1. Undoes the last commit but keeps the changes staged
2. Amends those changes into the previous commit

## Method 3: Reset and Recommit

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~2
git commit -m "New combined commit message"
```

This combines both commits into a single new commit.

## Important Notes

- **If you've already pushed**: You'll need to force push: `git push --force` (⚠️ use with caution on shared branches)
- **For unpushed commits**: All methods are safe
- **Preserve both messages**: In interactive rebase, use `squash` to combine messages, or `fixup` to discard the second message

Which method you choose depends on whether you want to edit the commit message and your personal preference!
